title: Schema-Validated LLM Workflows: A Benchmark Protocol and Comparative Evaluation Across Six Python Implementations
abstract: arXiv:2611.27106v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language models are increasingly used to extract records, generate SQL, summarize reports, answer policy questions, and route operational work. At these software boundaries, parseable output is necessary but does not establish task correctness. We present a reproducible benchmark protocol, a public executable artifact, and a confirmatory live API evaluation that separate structural validity from task-specific correctness across five business workflow tasks and six Python implementation conditions: PydanticAI, LangGraph, DSPy, CrewAI, Agno, and a framework-free SDK reference.   We hypothesize that (H1) schema validity and task quality are separable, (H2) structured-output binding paths are heterogeneous under a shared model and lowest-common-denominator contract, and (H3) condition-by-task interactions concentrate failures rather than shifting all tasks equally. translated_title: 模式验证的大语言模型工作流：一项基准测试协议与六种Python实现的对比评估
translated_abstract: 大语言模型正越来越多地被用于提取记录、生成SQL、汇总报告、回答政策问题以及分派运营工作。在这些软件边界上，输出可解析是必要条件，但并不能保证任务的正确性。我们提出了一个可复现的基准测试协议、一个公开的可执行工件，以及一项验证性的实时API评估，在五个业务工作流任务和六种Python实现条件（PydanticAI、LangGraph、DSPy、CrewAI、Agno，以及一个不依赖框架的SDK参考实现）下，将结构有效性（模式有效性）与任务特定正确性加以区分。我们提出以下假设：(H1) 模式有效性与任务质量是可分离的；(H2) 在共享模型与最小公约数契约的条件下，结构化输出的绑定路径是异构的；(H3) 条件与任务的交互效应会使失败集中于特定组合，而不是均匀地影响所有任务。验证性分析使用了各自独立的不同任务实例（100个提取任务实例……原文在此处截断）。
tldr: 该论文提出了一个可复现的基准测试协议与公开可执行工件，在五个业务工作流任务上对比六种Python实现，将LLM输出的模式有效性与任务正确性分离评估，并验证了两者可分离、结构化输出绑定路径异构、且失败集中于特定条件-任务组合这三大假设。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces a reproducible benchmark protocol and public executable artifact that disentangle schema validity from task-specific correctness across five business workflow tasks and six Python implementations (PydanticAI, LangGraph, DSPy, CrewAI, Agno, and a framework-free SDK), confirming that validity and quality are separable, structured-output binding paths are heterogeneous, and failures concentrate in specific condition-by-task interactions.
